title: k-means without a loop
summary: Three hundred points find their five clusters with no loop over points: every point's distance to every center is one table, the nearest center one reduce, the new centers means by group. A poor start gets stuck, a far-apart one does not. Ends on the live page.

scenes.heading: k-means, as arrays
scenes.narration: Three hundred points, five centers. Each step, every point picks its nearest center, and the centers move. There is no loop over the points.
lines: Each point in the color of its nearest center.

scenes.heading: 1. Every distance, one table
scenes.narration: First, the distance from every point to every center. One expression gives the whole table, a row for each point, a column for each center.
lines: Squared distances: a row a point, a column a center.
Ten of the points, two from each blob.

scenes.heading: 2. The nearest, one reduce
scenes.narration: Then the smallest number in each row marks the nearest center. One reduce finds it for every point, as rows of zeros and ones.

lines.xtl: l:a_ssign := { C X -> nn:a_rgmax n_eg X h:d_ist C }
O := (t_ally C) nn:o_neHot C l:a_ssign X

lines: The place of each row's smallest: its nearest center.

scenes.heading: 3. Means by group
scenes.narration: Turn that table on its side and multiply by the points. That adds up each group. Divide by the counts, and you have the new centers.

lines.xtl: (((o_\ O) '+ '* i_nner X) + C * f_loat n = 0.0) / 1.0 m_ax n

lines: O turned, times X: each group's sum. Over n: its mean.
A center with no points stays where it is.

scenes.heading: 4. Step, and repeat
scenes.narration: Now repeat the step. From a poor start, three centers crowd one blob and get stuck. From a far apart start, each center finds its own blob.

lines.xtl: C10 := 10 '{ C -> X ml:k_step C } p_ower C0

lines: Left, a poor start. Right, farthest first.
